newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI revises takeover code for companies.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI revises takeover code for companies.

text.p: Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Wednesday proposed amendments to the takeover code for companies.
"The requirement of minimum shareholdings after the offer has been modified and 100 percent offer would now be possible," SEBI said in a statment.
SEBI said the threshold for mandatory public offer has been retained at 10 percent of the total equity capital of a firm.
The market regulator proposed an extension of the timing for a competitive takeover bid to 21 days from 14 days.
Other recommendations include the imposition of elaborate disclosure requirements in the offer documents and permission to revise upwards the price or quantity of shares in the offer.
SEBI did not define takeovers but said a change in control would be a ground for a public offer.
It assigned greater responsibility to merchant bankers.
"The procedure for public announcements and the contents of public announcements have been elaborated and clarified.
SEBI said the final recommendations would be discussed at a meeting on September 28.
